messages:
Zane: Quick one  hiring an engineer based in the UK, start date 12/20. Candidate asked if unused sick days at end-of-year can be converted to a floating holiday or paid out. Also they want to swap the company-observed 12/26 holiday to 12/28 for travel. What's allowed across EMEA?

Olivia (People Ops): UK note first: statutory sick pay (SSP) and employment law can restrict how sick pay is handled. For W-2/UK payroll hires (PAYE), we generally do NOT convert statutory sick to cash or floating days. Any discretionary top-ups are possible but must be approved and recorded.

Priya (Hiring): Contractor vs employee difference? Offer needs exact wording.

Olivia (People Ops): Contractors (IR35/etc aside) are contract-specific. For employees on PAYE, include: "Sick leave follows UK statutory rules; unused statutory sick pay is not eligible for conversion. Any discretionary grants are subject to People Ops & Finance approval and payroll cutoffs." For contractors: say "subject to contract/SOW amendment and Legal review."

Noor (EMEA Ops): Practical EMEA payroll notes: if you want to offer a discretionary stipend, Finance will treat it as a taxable bonus. Payroll needs country, employee ID, and approval before the regional payroll close. For UK December payroll close: 12/10.

Carla (Payroll-EMEA): Confirmed. Also if the hire starts 12/20 we pro-rate holiday accruals. We cannot grant carryover for statutory entitlements automatically. If manager requests a discretionary carryover grant (company-funded), submit exception ticket with business justification and budget code.

Zane: Understood. About the holiday swap (12/26 -> 12/28): is that allowed? Candidate wants the company holiday moved due to travel.

Olivia (People Ops): Holiday swap rules vary by region. In the UK we allow swaps if it doesn't impact operations and manager approves. Manager must file the swap in the people-ops flow and People Ops will record the override. Deadline for year-end calendar changes: 12/01. If after that date, we can offer a discretionary floating day instead.

Priya (Hiring): Example offer language to use?

Olivia (People Ops): Use: "Holidays and sick leave comply with local law. Statutory sick entitlements are not convertible to paid time off or cash. Discretionary exceptions may be granted by People Ops and Finance and must be requested prior to payroll cutoff." Add a contractor clause if needed.

Legal (Counsel): Small legal flag: for UK hires, check continuous service start date if you're pro-rating or granting exceptions linked to tenure. Also ensure any discretionary grant doesn't create an implied contractual right. Add "subject to approval" language.

Zane: One more edge case: the candidate asked if the team can donate a couple of floating days to a colleague (compassion). Is donation allowed in UK?

Olivia (People Ops): We don't run a formal donation program in EMEA. For compassionate cases we prefer company-funded discretionary grants. Donor-to-donor transfers can be legally tricky in UK (employment law/tax). If team insists, Legal must review and donors must sign consent. Faster route: manager requests a discretionary grant (people-ops ticket) with budget code.

Carla (Payroll-EMEA): Adding: any discretionary grants will be processed as taxable pay in the country of employment unless we structure as additional paid leave in the HRIS (requires set-up). Payroll needs 5 business days lead time for overrides.

Zane: Great. I'll keep offer conservative and include exception path. I'll ask candidate if they'd accept company discretionary grant language instead of promise.

people-ops-bot: New exception ticket created: #HR-2230-814  attach manager approval and country of employment. People Ops triage ETA 2 business days.

Olivia (People Ops): Thanks. Zane  once candidate confirms, drop the proposed offer text and any requested amounts in the ticket and ping me. I'll coordinate Payroll + Legal for UK specifics. :white_check_mark:
